question.text: For diatomic molecules, the correct statement(s) about the molecular orbitals formed by the overlap of two <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">z</mi></msub></math> orbitals is(are)

options.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>σ</mi></math> orbital has a total of two nodal planes.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>σ</mi><mo>*</mo></msup></math> orbital has one node in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>xz</mi></math>-plane containing the molecular axis.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi></math> orbital has one node in the plane which is perpendicular to the molecular axis and goes through the center of the molecule

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi><mo>*</mo></msup></math> orbital has one node in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>xy</mi></math>-plane containing the molecular axis.

solution.text: When this orbital combine along the internuclear axis then σ orbital is formed while this orbital approach each other parallel to each other and perpendicular to the internuclear axis π orbital is formed.
